## What I added (only under `tests/`, plus a `.venv`)

```
tests/
├── conftest.py          # puts the repo root on sys.path so the `pytest` console script can import highground
├── test_risk.py         # 13 tests
├── test_replay.py       # 12 tests
├── test_feeds.py        # 25 tests
└── test_briefing.py     # 6 tests
```

- **`test_risk.py`** — `assess()` determinism/purity (same inputs → identical `Risk`, inputs not mutated, score independent of `as_of`); dry/no-zone block → `low` (score 0.0); 50 mm/3 h on a 100-yr block with storm history → `high` (score ≈ 2.15, and the same rain on a bare block stays `low`); Flood Warning adds exactly +1.0 to `h` and raises the score; flood reports raise `c` per `0.6·e^(−age/3)` and decay with age; reasons carry the expected codes with receipt-friendly `value`/`unit` (40.0 mm, 4 reports, 7.2 ft, 65 km/h …) and every numeric value appears in the JSON facts blob; `level_for` pinned at all four thresholds (0.8/2.0/3.5).
- **`test_replay.py`** — synthetic dataset: 3 cells from `geo.cell` + one k-ring neighbor (chosen to share C1's weather point so counts are deterministic), hourly weather rows for all 5 `geo.POINTS` with unique rain amounts (11/13/17/101 mm) so look-ahead is detectable, 8 timestamped reports, 2 NWS products, 3 tide rows. No-look-ahead is verified three ways: an rain hour counts only once it has ended (16:30Z → 24 mm, 17:00Z → 41 mm, the 101 mm hour invisible until 19:00Z), reports never appear with negative age and the 6 h window is strict (17:00:00 report excluded at 23:00Z, 17:00:01 included), NWS products count only once issued and while valid. A 15-minute sweep recomputes rain from ended-hours-only and asserts all report ages ≥ 0. `backtest()` returns exactly the 12 expected keys with pinned counts (3 blocks with reports, 2 flagged, 1 before/at report with 120 min median lead, 1 after, 1 never, 0 false alarms, first flag 15:00Z, first report 17:00Z) and is deterministic across runs.
- **`test_feeds.py`** — parses every fixture: all 60 `open311_sewer.json` rows (ids `311:<id>`, keyword categories, h3 cell, double-parse identical), `datasf_311_20221231.json` (12 of 25 rows survive; Pacific→UTC conversion asserted exactly; subtype mapping; rejections), `nws_docs` on `nws_alerts.json`, `iem_docs` on `iem_mtr_20221231.json` (window/zone/VTEC filters, dedup, empty window → []), `tide_docs` on both NOAA files (48 obs + 8 predictions, missing `v` skipped), `weather_docs` on both Open-Meteo files (ids, points, forecast flag), `chp_docs` on `chp_ggcc.xml` (exactly the 2 SF hazard logs; synthetic XML checks filtering and the flooding flag). `merge()` keeps the stronger `category_source` (datasf > mistral > service_code > keywords, ties → newer) while the newest `status`/`updated_at` always lands, and derived keys (`zone_100yr`, `slr24`, `zones`) are never stored.
- **`test_briefing.py`** — `receipts()` drops the sentence with the invented "99 mm", keeps sentences citing 42.5 mm / 2 reports / 1,234 sandbags / 7 reports, always allows 1/311/911, and drops a sentence if *any* of its numbers is unknown.

## Notes

- **No source bugs found** — I changed nothing under `highground/`; the six initial failures were all wrong expectations in my own tests (e.g. CHP "3:15PM" on 2026-11-03 is 23:15Z PST; "overflowing" classifies as `flooding` because the flood regex is checked first; `level_for(-1)` can't occur since every score component is ≥ 0).
- I created `.venv` (gitignored) from `/usr/local/bin/python3` with `--system-site-packages` plus a venv-local pytest install, because the bare `pytest` on PATH (`/root/.local/bin/pytest`) runs under `/usr/bin/python3`, which has no `h3`/`httpx`. So use `.venv/bin/pytest -q` (or `PATH=.venv/bin:$PATH pytest -q`); `python3 -m pytest -q` from the repo root also passes.
- Assumption I relied on: replay NWS timestamps must be `"…Z"`-format ISO strings (as `build_dataset`/`iem_docs` produce) because `Replay.inputs` compares them lexically against `z(t)` — the synthetic dataset follows that format.
